Annotation

Annotate viral genomes, characterize functions, and curate sequences for downstream ecology.

Stage 8 of the Viral Metagenome Workflow. Click Annotation & AMGs for the walkthrough, or a neighboring stage to browse its tools.

Viral genome annotation assigns putative functions to predicted genes by comparing them against curated reference databases. Beyond basic gene prediction, annotation tools like DRAM-v specifically identify auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs) — viral genes co-opted from host metabolism that can influence biogeochemical cycles. Annotation results are also used to manually screen viral contigs for false positives and to prepare sequences for database submission.
Tool Description Platforms Links Reference
DRAM-v Distills viral genome annotation into structured metabolic profiles, identifying auxiliary metabolic genes (AMGs) and their ecological relevance. HPC CyVerse Docs · Official Shaffer et al., Nucleic Acids Res (2020)
Cenote-Taker 2 Automates virus discovery and sequence annotation by detecting hallmark genes, curating genomes, and preparing sequences for GenBank submission. HPC CyVerse Docs coming soon · Official Tisza et al., Virus Evol (2021)
VIGA Viral genome annotation pipeline for prokaryotic viruses, and can generate GenBank-compatible output from assembled contigs. HPC Docs · Official Tortuero et al., PeerJ (2018)
PhageTerm Determines phage genome termini and packaging mechanisms (cos sites, pac sites, DTR/ITR) from sequencing read depth at genome ends — useful for correctly circularizing and orienting phage assemblies. HPC Docs · Official Garneau et al., Scientific Reports (2017)
Pharokka A rapid standardized annotation tool for bacteriophage genomes and metagenomes. Predicts genes with PHANOTATE by default (Prodigal and prodigal-gv optional) and assigns functions against the PHROGs, CARD and VFDB databases. HPC Docs coming soon · Official Bouras et al., Bioinformatics (2023)
